title: heterogeneous-edge-bom-and-utilization-simulator-2026
description: Working spreadsheet for simulating heterogeneous GPU fleets across edge / regional VPC deployments. Includes multiple procurement scenarios, utilization curves, rack/power estimates, and quick cost/lead-time trade-offs. Informal working doc: assumptions, scratch calculations, TODOs for procurement team.
version_notes: v0.3 - added H100 and L4 mix scenarios, included rack-level power derate; v0.2 - initial sim with A100 and p99 latency-constraint column; v0.1 - skeleton metrics and columns.
assumptions: 1) Target P99 latency budget per region expressed in ms; 2) Models split into latency-sensitive (chat) and batch (embeddings); 3) H100 gives ~1.8x throughput vs A100 for KV-cache heavy workloads; 4) Edge racks limited to 60A PDUs -> ~24kW usable per rack; 5) Spare GPU spare pool sized as 5% of active fleet + 2 hot-standby nodes; 6) Procurement lead-times vary: H100 (12-16 weeks), A100 (8-12 weeks), L4 (6-10 weeks); 7) Power/cooling overhead 1.2x nameplate for data center planning; 8) Price estimates are list-price estimates for BOM guidance only.

open_questions_and_todos: - Validate current H100 pricing with partner; - Confirm edge rack PDU constraints for partner sites (AP and EU); - Decide policy for mixing H100 + L4 vs homogeneous for SLO simplification; - Add latency-sensitivity weighting per model family; - Hook up to procurement price CSV and live lead-time API; - Run sensitivity analysis for utilization range 40-80%
notes_and_comments: Quick notes: packing efficiency assumptions are optimistic for embeddings workload when using continuous batching; for chat p99 targets we assume KV hot-cache hit rate >= 70% to hit latency budgets; consider dedicated small instance class for very low concurrency customers to avoid fragmentation.
